Now I can make my assessment. Comparing the test image to the references:

**Test image key features:**
- Extensive white/gray cottony mold covering a large central area of the ear (husks pulled back)
- A distinct **dark green** patch in the center of the white mold area
- Yellow kernels visible at edges, still relatively healthy
- Mold appears to grow between and over kernels

**Analysis of candidates:**
- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: White mold starting from base, brownish kernels — test image has green, doesn't match well
- **Fusarium**: White/pink mold on scattered kernels — the scale of coverage doesn't match as well, and no green
- **Ear_rots_Trichoderma**: Dark green mold between kernels with white mycelium phase — the test image shows white (unsporulated mycelium) and the dark green patch (sporulating area), consistent with Trichoderma's lifecycle of white hyphae → dark green spores
- **Ear_rots_Aspergillus**: Olive-green powdery mold — the green in the test image is darker/more teal-green than olive

The Trichoderma reference images confirm this pattern: green patches on kernels with white/lighter mycelium, and the description mentions "dark green powdery spores and dark green mold growing between kernels, often covering the entire ear."
